task_context.problem_statement: Let $f(x) = (x+2)^2-5$. If the domain of $f$ is all real numbers, then $f$ does not have an inverse function, but if we restrict the domain of $f$ to an interval $[c,\infty)$, then $f$ may have an inverse function. What is the smallest value of $c$ we can use here, so that $f$ does have an inverse function?

It has to be one-to-one, meaning it passes the horizontal line test. But I don't have time to sketch this out. Just tell me the value of c!

Since you're dealing with a quadratic function, you have a parabola. A parabola is symmetric, which is why it fails the horizontal line test over all real numbers. To make it one-to-one, you need to restrict the domain to a part of the graph that is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing. Where does the function change direction?
That's the vertex. The vertex for $(x+2)^2-5$ is at $x = -2$. So if I start the domain at -2, it's just the right side of the curve. Is c = -2?

You've correctly identified the vertex. To determine if that is the smallest possible value for $c$, consider what happens if you pick a value slightly to the left of the vertex. Would the function still be one-to-one on the interval $[c, \infty)$?

No, because then you'd have a piece of the descending part and a piece of the ascending part, so a horizontal line would hit it twice. So -2 is the smallest. Just tell me if I'm right so I can submit!
